scenario: A long-time membrane or laptop-keyboard user is considering a first mechanical keyboard and wants mechanism-first homework rather than a color chart or a blanket upgrade claim. The available material includes membrane-contact and keyboard-matrix references, a Cherry MX family reference, four current catalog snapshots spanning full-size and compact layouts and several switch labels, and community discussions with conflicting first-hand experiences.
target: Explain how a physical press becomes a registered keycode, distinguish switch feel from matrix detection, and describe the common Cherry MX Red, Brown, and Blue categories without turning color into a cross-manufacturer standard. Then compare the frozen full-size and compact configurations and the conflicting community experiences to produce a first-purchase process based on exact layout, connectivity, noise, switch maker and model, hot-swap, budget, and hands-on trial. State what the material cannot prove about speed, accuracy, universal switch behavior, and a best board.
